title: Introducing peer support workers into an early intervention in psychosis service: a single-arm feasibility study with embedded interviews
abstract: Aim: to assess whether peer support can be introduced and evaluated in an early intervention service well enough to justify a definitive trial. Design: single-arm feasibility study in 2027 with progression criteria for uptake, retention, delivery and questionnaire completion, and interviews with young people, families and staff. Results will be reported after the study year.
introduction: A quarter of young people disengage from early intervention services within a year. Peer support is associated with better engagement, but uptake, retention and the sustainability of the peer role are uncertain.
methods: Eligible young people were offered peer support in a fixed order. Uptake, retention, contacts and questionnaire completion were measured against pre-set thresholds; peer worker wellbeing was checked monthly; interviews explored how the role was taken up.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present uptake, retention, delivery, completion and peer worker wellbeing against the progression thresholds, and the interview themes.
discussion: The discussion will state whether each progression criterion was met and what changes a trial would need.
limitations: Single service, no comparison group, small numbers.
conclusion: To be written after the study; it will not claim effects on engagement.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies (adapted) and COREQ
summary: Feasibility-structured draft with results left empty.
